"Expiry Warning (hours)" only controls how early students see the expiring-soon notice; notifications, shutdown and deletion after expiry are handled by the TTL lifecycle on the "Resource Policies" page.
UserGuide.scheduler.save.title: Save when you are done
UserGuide.scheduler.save.text: All cards share the "Save Scheduling Settings" button below, which is only available after a change. "Restore" discards unsaved changes. If you leave the page with unsaved changes, you will be asked to confirm first.
UserGuide.governance.title: Resource Policies
UserGuide.governance.intro.title: The platform's automatic governance rules
UserGuide.governance.intro.text: The upper "Governance" section holds the automatic rules the scheduler runs periodically: resource alerts, expiry reclamation, idle shutdown, anti-mining, snapshot cleanup and clone concurrency. The lower "Quotas" section limits how many resources each user may use.
UserGuide.governance.alerts.title: Resource usage alerts
UserGuide.governance.alerts.text: When a node's or machine's CPU, memory or disk usage crosses a threshold, an alert event is created; the same metric on the same target is not raised again within the cooldown. Email is only sent to administrators when "Email Notifications" is ticked.
UserGuide.governance.ttl.title: How expired machines are reclaimed
UserGuide.governance.ttl.text: With "Enable TTL Reclamation" ticked, owners are emailed before expiry according to "Warn Before Expiry (days)", the machine shuts down automatically when it expires, and it is only deleted after the "Deletion Grace Period (days)", which counts from the expiry shutdown.
UserGuide.governance.idle.title: Shut down idle machines automatically
UserGuide.governance.idle.text: A machine counts as idle only after it has stayed on with average CPU below the threshold for the full observation window. The owner is notified after the idle-notification hours, and the machine shuts down once the shutdown grace period ends — it is never deleted. The notification time must be shorter than the grace period.
UserGuide.governance.mining.title: Anti-mining detection
UserGuide.governance.mining.text: Machines whose CPU stays above the threshold throughout the observation window are treated as suspected mining. With "Auto Snapshot & Suspend" on, a snapshot is saved before the machine is suspended; with it off, only an incident is recorded. Accounts are never suspended automatically — an administrator confirms that under "Resource Monitoring → Mining Incidents".
UserGuide.governance.save.title: Governance settings save together
UserGuide.governance.save.text: Every governance card above, including VM / LXC auto-detection, snapshot governance and clone concurrency, shares "Save Governance Settings", which is only available after a change. "Restore" discards unsaved changes. The quotas below are saved separately.
UserGuide.governance.quotaGlobal.title: Global default quota
UserGuide.governance.quotaGlobal.text: Users without a personal override get these limits for CPU cores, memory, disk and instances; ticking "Unlimited" removes the limit. Changes only affect later creation and resizing, not existing resources. This card has its own "Save" button.
UserGuide.governance.quotaOverrides.text: For someone who needs different limits, click "Add Quota", pick the user and set their own limits; the fields start from the current global defaults. Users with an override use those numbers instead, and deleting the override returns them to the global defaults.
UserGuide.ldap.title: LDAP
UserGuide.ldap.intro.title: Sign in with campus directory accounts
UserGuide.ldap.intro.text: This page configures LDAP / Active Directory sign-in. Once enabled, the login page gains a "Campus Account" tab where users sign in with their school directory username and password.
UserGuide.ldap.login.title: Server address and enabling
UserGuide.ldap.login.text: Enter an ldap:// or ldaps:// address as the server URI. With ldap://, ticking "Use StartTLS" is recommended for encryption; ldaps:// does not need it. Confirm the setup with "Test Connection" below before ticking "Enable LDAP Login".
UserGuide.ldap.service.title: Service account and user search
UserGuide.ldap.service.text: The platform first binds to the directory with the service account (Bind DN), finds the user under the "User Search Base DN" using the "User Filter Template", and then verifies the password they entered. {username} in the template is replaced with the username typed at sign-in. Leave the service account password blank to keep the current one.
UserGuide.ldap.roles.title: Account creation and role mapping
UserGuide.ldap.roles.text: With "Auto-create Accounts" ticked, an account is created automatically the first time someone signs in through LDAP, as a student by default; members of the teacher or administrator group DN get that role instead. LDAP accounts are re-mapped from their groups at every sign-in, so a role changed manually in User Management will be overwritten. If no administrator group is set, existing admins are not demoted.
UserGuide.ldap.actions.title: Test before you save
UserGuide.ldap.actions.text: "Test Connection" uses the values currently in the form, including unsaved changes, to check whether the service account can bind to the directory; it saves nothing. "Save LDAP Settings" is only available after a change, and "Restore" discards unsaved changes.
UserGuide.storage.title: Storage
UserGuide.storage.intro.title: Storage settings used for placement
UserGuide.storage.intro.text: This page lists the storage synced from each PVE connection. When creating a machine, the platform uses the enabled state, speed tier and priority here to decide which storage holds its disk. The list only updates when you click "Sync" on the "PVE Management" page.
UserGuide.storage.filters.title: Filter and search
UserGuide.storage.filters.text: Switch between "All", "Enabled" and "Disabled"; the numbers on the buttons are the counts for each state. The search box matches storage name, node, connection name or type.
UserGuide.storage.row.title: Storage details
UserGuide.storage.row.text: The node is shown next to the name; shared storage shows "Shared · N nodes", and changes here apply to every node it is mounted on. The second line shows the type, used / total capacity (GB) and purposes — only storage marked VM or LXC is chosen for that kind of machine's disk.
UserGuide.storage.speed.title: Speed tier is compared first
UserGuide.storage.speed.text: Placement first picks the fastest speed tier (NVMe → SSD → HDD → Unknown) and then compares usage. Newly synced storage defaults to "Unknown", so remember to set the correct tier. Your choice is saved immediately.
UserGuide.storage.priority.title: User priority
UserGuide.storage.priority.text: Enter 1–10; lower numbers come first, and priority only breaks ties when speed tier and usage are about the same. The value is saved when you press Enter or move focus away, and out-of-range values revert automatically.
UserGuide.storage.enabled.title: Disabled storage is never chosen
UserGuide.storage.enabled.text: Untick "Enabled" and placement will no longer put new machines' disks on this storage. Toggling the box saves immediately.
UserGuide.monitoring.title: Resource Monitoring
UserGuide.monitoring.intro.title: Live status of the platform and clusters
UserGuide.monitoring.intro.text: This page brings together platform component health, PVE cluster usage, active alerts and mining incidents, refreshing about every 30 seconds. It only collects and displays status; an administrator has to come here to look into problems.
UserGuide.monitoring.grafana.title: Detailed metrics in Grafana
UserGuide.monitoring.grafana.text: "View details in Grafana" appears only when the monitoring stack is enabled. It signs you in to Grafana as an administrator so you can browse longer-term metrics and dashboards. If the button is missing, the monitoring stack is not enabled.
UserGuide.monitoring.health.title: See at a glance what is down
UserGuide.monitoring.health.text: The top row shows the status and response time of components such as the database, Redis, the background worker, each PVE connection and the Gateway. Click the title bar to expand the scheduled task details: last run, last success, failures in a row and the last error for each task, with problem tasks listed first.
UserGuide.monitoring.overview.title: Cluster usage overview
UserGuide.monitoring.overview.text: CPU, memory and disk usage summed across all PVE connections, next to the number of online nodes and running VMs and LXCs (the number after the slash is the total). If PVE cannot be reached, an error appears here instead, but system health and alerts are still shown.
UserGuide.monitoring.alerts.title: Active alerts
UserGuide.monitoring.alerts.text: Lists alerts for usage over thresholds (cluster, node, VM) and for platform health problems, labelled with the cluster when there are several. "Acknowledge" only marks an alert as seen; it stays on the list until the condition clears. Thresholds are set on the "Resource Policies" page.
UserGuide.monitoring.mining.title: Mining incidents need a human decision
UserGuide.monitoring.mining.text: Machines whose CPU stays maxed out for a long time get an evidence snapshot and are suspended automatically, then wait here for an administrator. "Ban" disables the owner's account and keeps the machine suspended; "Dismiss as False Positive" tries to resume the machine and can add it to the exemption list so it is not checked again. The number on the tab is the count of open incidents.
UserGuide.monitoring.nodes.title: Usage per node
UserGuide.monitoring.nodes.text: Click the title bar to collapse or expand the whole card; the choice is remembered in this browser. Click an online node's row to expand its CPU and memory trend for the last day. Offline nodes have no trend data and cannot be expanded.
UserGuide.monitoring.top.title: The heaviest machines
UserGuide.monitoring.top.text: Shows the top 5 running VMs / LXCs by CPU and by memory, with their VMID and node, so you can find the machines slowing a node down.
UserGuide.ipManagement.title: IP Management
UserGuide.ipManagement.intro.title: Where machine IPs come from
UserGuide.ipManagement.intro.text: When a VM / LXC is created, the platform automatically assigns it a static IP from the subnet configured here. This page manages that subnet configuration and lists every address in use and what it is used for.
UserGuide.ipManagement.createSubnet.text: Until a subnet is configured, no one on the site can create a VM / LXC. Click "Create Subnet Config" and enter the subnet CIDR, gateway IP, bridge name and Gateway VM IP; addresses start being assigned once it is saved.
UserGuide.ipManagement.editSubnet.title: Adjust the subnet config
UserGuide.ipManagement.editSubnet.text: You can change the CIDR, gateway, bridge, VLAN, DNS, the external port pool and entry host for course environments, and the default blocked subnets. The CIDR is locked while machines or class reservations use the range; the VLAN only affects machines created later; blocked subnets are applied machine by machine after saving, and any VMIDs that fail are reported.
UserGuide.ipManagement.stats.title: Total, available and allocated
UserGuide.ipManagement.stats.text: "Allocated" covers machines, gateways and every kind of reservation; "Available" is what can still be given to new machines. Once it reaches zero, no new machines can be created.
UserGuide.ipManagement.toolbar.title: Search and the current subnet
UserGuide.ipManagement.toolbar.text: Search by IP, VMID or description. On the right you can see the subnet CIDR, bridge and VLAN currently in effect.
UserGuide.ipManagement.table.title: Who each IP belongs to
UserGuide.ipManagement.table.text: "Purpose" shows where the address went: VM, LXC, Gateway VM, Gateway, Reserved, or IPs set aside in advance for classes and quick practice. The table is read-only; IPs are released automatically when machines are deleted. 50 rows per page.
UserGuide.audit.title: Audit Log
UserGuide.audit.intro.title: Who did what, and when
UserGuide.audit.intro.text: Records sign-ins, machine operations, settings changes and other actions, with the user, details, VMID and source IP. For actions run automatically, such as scheduled jobs, the user column shows "System".
UserGuide.audit.summary.title: Summary for the period
UserGuide.audit.summary.text: Total records, dangerous actions, failed sign-ins and active users. These four numbers only follow the start and end dates; search, action and user filters do not affect them.
UserGuide.audit.filters.title: Combine filters
UserGuide.audit.filters.text: The search box matches action details and IPs and runs on its own once you stop typing; you can also filter by action type, user and date range. Dates cannot be in the future, and if the start is later than the end the other side moves to match. "Clear" brings everything back.
UserGuide.audit.export.title: Export to CSV
UserGuide.audit.export.text: "Export CSV" exports what the current filters match, up to 10000 entries. With no filters set you are asked to confirm first, because the file can be large.
UserGuide.audit.table.title: Record by record
UserGuide.audit.table.text: Newest first, 50 per page. Long "Details" are cut off; hover over them to read the full text.
UserGuide.jobs.title: Background Tasks
UserGuide.jobs.intro.title: Progress of long-running work
UserGuide.jobs.intro.text: VM request provisioning, spec changes, deletions, machine templates, resets, batch provisioning, backups and restores all run in the background, and their progress is collected here. Administrators see every task on the site; everyone else sees only their own. Only the last 30 days are listed, and the page refreshes automatically.
UserGuide.jobs.stats.title: Counted from the current filter
UserGuide.jobs.stats.text: The in-progress, completed and failed counts are calculated from the list currently filtered below, not from the whole site.
UserGuide.jobs.kindFilter.title: Filter by type
UserGuide.jobs.kindFilter.text: Show only one kind of task, for example only "Deletion" or "Batch provisioning". Choose "All Types" to go back.
UserGuide.jobs.statusFilter.title: Filter by status
UserGuide.jobs.statusFilter.text: "In Progress" covers Pending, Running and Blocked. "Blocked" means the task is waiting on a person, for example an approved spec change that the applicant still has to apply.
UserGuide.jobs.table.title: Click a row for details
UserGuide.jobs.table.text: Each row shows the task name, type, status, progress and applicant. Click any row to open its details: created, updated and completed times, the message, detail fields and error output. While the task is still running, the details refresh every 3 seconds.
UserGuide.gateway.title: Gateway VM
UserGuide.gateway.intro.title: Manage the public-facing Gateway VM
UserGuide.gateway.intro.text: The Gateway VM uses nginx for port forwarding, machine domains and the platform entry, and runs the WireGuard VPN; the platform manages it entirely over SSH. For first-time setup, complete "Connection Settings" and then "Install services"; set up the certificate and platform entry when you need HTTPS.
UserGuide.gateway.sshForm.title: SSH connection settings
UserGuide.gateway.sshForm.text: Enter the Gateway's Host / IP, SSH port and user, then click "Save Settings". "Test Connection" tests the saved settings, so save your changes first. Use "Reset Host Key" only after the Gateway has been reinstalled or replaced.
UserGuide.gateway.sshKey.title: Add the public key to the Gateway
UserGuide.gateway.sshKey.text: Click "Regenerate Keypair" to create the platform's own key, then "Copy" the public key into the Gateway's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. Regenerating invalidates the old key immediately, so the new public key has to be added again.
UserGuide.gateway.install.title: One-click install of Gateway services
UserGuide.gateway.install.text: "One-click install" installs nginx, WireGuard and the monitoring exporters on the Gateway in the background and enables UFW. It takes a few minutes and you can leave this page. The SSH account must be root or able to sudo without a password; when it finishes, domain and port forwarding rules are synced back to the Gateway automatically.
UserGuide.gateway.certificate.title: Bring your own HTTPS certificate
UserGuide.gateway.certificate.text: Certificates are not issued automatically: put the fullchain and private key on the Gateway yourself, enter their full paths and click "Save and apply". The platform entry and every machine domain share this one certificate. To renew, overwrite the files at the same paths and click "Apply again"; the card below shows the expiry date and covered domains.
UserGuide.gateway.platform.title: Serve the platform through the Gateway
UserGuide.gateway.platform.text: Tick the option to enable it, then enter the platform domain and a deployment host address the Gateway can reach. "Test upstream" only checks whether the Gateway can reach the platform and saves nothing; "Save and apply" probes first and then writes it into nginx. If the domain is not in a zone managed in Cloudflare, you have to update DNS yourself; the remaining to-dos are listed in the card below.
UserGuide.gateway.nginx.title: nginx status and main config
UserGuide.gateway.nginx.text: At the top you can start, stop, restart or Reload nginx; stopping it cuts every forwarded connection. The editor only opens /etc/nginx/nginx.conf: "Write Config" runs nginx -t first and restores the old file if it fails, but the change does not take effect until you press Reload. Forwarding rules generated by SkyLab are not edited here.
UserGuide.gateway.wireguard.title: WireGuard VPN status
UserGuide.gateway.wireguard.text: Shows the VPN service status, authorized sessions, loaded peers, handshakes in the last 3 minutes and traffic, plus a summary of the tunnel settings, with the service log below. This page never returns any private key or peer public key.
